annotation_description: With a hand full of reactive spells (Spell Snare, Into the Flood Maw, Burst Lightning) and no early proactive plays, this is a classic control/tempo hand that benefits from drawing first. Going second gives an extra card, which is valuable for a deck that wants to trade resources efficiently. The hand has no 1-drop creature to leverage being on the play, and the only proactive early play is potentially a turn 2 Abandon Attachments (which doesn't benefit from being on the play). The Eddymurk Crab wants more instants/sorceries in the graveyard, which is easier to accumulate with an extra card.

Riverpyre Verge can only tap for U if you control an Island or Mountain. Playing it turn 1 with no other lands means it can only tap for R this turn. If the player plays Island turn 2, Verge will then be able to tap for U as well. However, playing Island first would let the player cast Opt on turn 1 (which is a U instant they have in hand), giving them a scry+draw to improve their position. By playing Riverpyre Verge first, they can only produce R mana this turn, which doesn't cast any of their 1-mana spells (Opt and Into the Flood Maw both cost U).

Kimi25 Truth missed their land drop on turn 3 with 4 lands in hand. They have Frostcliff Siege (a key 3-mana enchantment) ready to cast on turn 3 if they play a land, giving them either card advantage or a tempo boost. Instead, they declined to play any land, leaving themselves with only 2 mana available. This means Frostcliff Siege cannot be cast this turn, delaying their game plan by at least a full turn. Additionally, they will have to discard to hand size at end of turn (going from 8 to 7), wasting a card unnecessarily when they could have played a land to stay at 7.

message: Select card to discard (selected 0 of 2, min 2)
annotation_description: Discarded Riverpyre Verge (their 4th land) when stuck on 3 lands with expensive spells in hand. Missing the 4th land drop delays casting multiple spells per turn and accessing harmonize/kicker costs. They had redundant bounce spells (Into the Flood Maw, Bounce Off) and a duplicate Winternight Stories that were lower value discards.

With only 2 lands in play on turn 4 and needing to hit land drops, discarding a land is questionable. More importantly, Winternight Stories has harmonize ({4}{U}), meaning it can be cast from the graveyard later. Discarding Winternight Stories would effectively cost almost nothing since it's recoverable, while the Mountain is a permanent loss of a needed land drop.

Cast Stormchaser's Talent before playing a land. While the land can still be played afterward this turn, best practice is to play lands first to maximize available mana for potential responses or follow-up plays. With 3 Islands in hand, there's no reason to delay the land drop.

KimiK2 Valley has 8 cards in hand and will need to discard to 7 at end of turn. They have 3 mana available (Riverpyre Verge, Island, Island) and the opponent's Island is tapped, meaning the opponent likely can't counter spells. This was an opportunity to use instant-speed interaction before end of turn to avoid discarding. Specifically, they could cast Into the Flood Maw (1 mana) to bounce the opponent's Otter Token (removing a threat and the Stormchaser's Talent value engine), which would get them down to 7 cards without wasting a discard. Alternatively, Bounce Off could bounce the Otter. Instead, they passed and had to discard a card for free.

Discarded Spirebluff Canal (a needed dual land) instead of a redundant Winternight Stories. KimiK2 Valley has only 3 lands on board and needs mana development. Winternight Stories has Harmonize, meaning it can be cast from the graveyard, making it the ideal discard. They already have one copy in the graveyard and two in hand.

Kimi25 Truth has 8 cards in hand and needs to discard to 7. Instead of playing a land (they have 3 Islands and a Spirebluff Canal in hand, with only 2 lands on the battlefield), they chose to pass and discard. Playing a land would have developed their mana while still getting down to 7 cards naturally, avoiding the waste of discarding a card. With Frostcliff Siege (3 mana), Winternight Stories (3 mana), and Boomerang Basics (1 mana) in hand, getting to 3 lands is important for casting these spells next turn.

Into the Flood Maw costs {U} and returns a target creature an opponent controls to their hand (or a nonland permanent if gifting a Fish). The opponent has a tapped Otter Token (1/1 with prowess) and Stormchaser's Talent (a Class enchantment). Bouncing the Otter Token is low-value since it's just a token and will cease to exist when returned to hand. However, if the gift is promised, you can target the Stormchaser's Talent instead, which is much more impactful - but that gives the opponent a 1/1 Fish token. The real issue is sequencing: casting Into the Flood Maw before playing Riverpyre Verge from hand wastes a potential land drop this turn. With Riverpyre Verge played first, you'd have 5 mana available, opening up more options. Additionally, Sleight of Hand should generally be cast before making other decisions to maximize information. Bouncing a token that will just cease to exist is fine value (removing a creature for 1 mana), but the sequencing of not playing the land first is a minor error.

message: Promise an opponent a tapped Fish?
annotation_description: The opponent cast Into the Flood Maw with Gift a tapped Fish, targeting one of KimiK2 Valley's nonland permanents to return to hand. KimiK2 Valley is choosing which of their opponent's permanents gets bounced. Stormchaser's Talent is a Class enchantment that already created an Otter token and can be leveled up to provide recurring value (level 2 returns an instant/sorcery from graveyard, level 3 creates tokens on every instant/sorcery cast). The Otter Token is just a 1/1 with prowess that can be easily recreated. Bouncing Stormchaser's Talent would force the opponent to re-spend mana to replay it and re-level it, setting them back significantly. Bouncing the Otter Token removes a trivial threat that Stormchaser's Talent can replace.

The opponent cast Into the Flood Maw targeting KimiK2 Valley's Otter Token (which was the opponent's Stormchaser's Talent token on their board - wait, looking more carefully, the Otter Token is on Kimi25 Truth's battlefield). Actually, re-reading: Into the Flood Maw returns a creature an opponent controls to hand - so it's targeting something KimiK2 Valley controls. But KimiK2 Valley has no creatures on the battlefield. The Otter Token is on Kimi25 Truth's side. Wait - the result says 'KimiK2 Valley puts Otter Token from battlefield into its owner's hand' - this means the opponent bounced the Otter Token back to its owner's (Kimi25 Truth's) hand, but it was on Kimi25 Truth's battlefield. Actually, looking at the After line, Into the Flood Maw was gifted (Fish token created) and used to bounce the Otter Token. Since the gift was promised, it returns a nonland permanent - the opponent bounced their own Otter Token? No - Into the Flood Maw says 'return target creature an opponent controls' or with gift 'return target nonland permanent an opponent controls.' KimiK2 Valley has no creatures/nonland permanents visible. Wait - actually I don't think KimiK2 Valley had a choice here. The opponent was casting Into the Flood Maw and KimiK2 Valley could respond with Bounce Off or Burst Lightning. The key question is: could KimiK2 Valley have responded productively? They could have cast Burst Lightning targeting the Otter Token (1/1 prowess) to kill it before it gets bounced back to hand. By not responding, the opponent gets to rebuy the Otter Token to hand (it's a token, so it ceases to exist - actually tokens that return to hand cease to exist). So the bounce actually removes the Otter Token permanently. This means the opponent is spending a card to remove their own token, which is bad for them. KimiK2 Valley was correct to let it resolve - no blunder here.

Eddymurk Crab costs only 1 blue mana (7 base minus 6 instant/sorcery cards in graveyard: Opt, Glacial Dragonhunt, Abandon Attachments, Winternight Stories, Into the Flood Maw, Sleight of Hand). KimiK2 Valley had 2 untapped lands capable of producing blue mana, so they could easily cast the 5/5 Crab and still have mana left over. The model incorrectly believed the Crab cost 7 mana.

KimiK2 Valley has 6 instant/sorcery cards in graveyard, reducing Eddymurk Crab's cost from {5}{U}{U} to just {U}{U}. They have exactly {U}{U} available from untapped Island and Riverpyre Verge. Deploying a 5/5 creature for 2 mana during their own combat (where it enters untapped) is an extremely strong play. They mistakenly thought they had nothing to do because they had no creatures, not realizing they could flash in the Crab.

KimiK2 Valley has 8 instants/sorceries in the graveyard, making Eddymurk Crab cost 5UU - 8 = just UU (2 mana). With 4 lands available (Riverpyre Verge and Island untapped, plus Steam Vents and Island tapped), they have at least 2 untapped lands capable of producing UU. The Eddymurk Crab is a 5/5 that would tap up to two of the opponent's creatures on entry, and it's a massive threat that should be deployed immediately. Additionally, Burst Lightning could kill the Fish token (dealing 2 damage to a 1/1). Passing the turn without deploying the Crab or using any of the available mana is a significant waste of tempo.

Playing Riverpyre Verge now means the Spirebluff Canal in hand will enter tapped next turn (3 other lands > 2). Playing Spirebluff Canal this turn while they have exactly 2 other lands would guarantee it enters untapped, and Riverpyre Verge always enters untapped regardless of land count.

Casting Frostcliff Siege on turn 7 with only a single 1/1 Fish token on board is a reasonable long-term investment, but Winternight Stories would draw 3 cards and help dig for more threats/answers immediately. The Siege needs creatures dealing combat damage (Jeskai) or creatures to buff (Temur) to generate value, and with just a 1/1 Fish token that's fairly anemic. Additionally, casting the Siege before playing a land drop is suboptimal - there are two Islands in hand and a Spirebluff Canal. Playing a land first preserves more options.

In an Izzet prowess/Otter token deck with Stormchaser's Talent, Temur mode on Frostcliff Siege is generally stronger because haste on Otter tokens created by Stormchaser's Talent (and future spells) provides immediate pressure. The +1/+0 and trample also synergize well with prowess creatures. Jeskai requires creatures to connect in combat to draw, which is conditional.

Cast Winternight Stories before playing a land drop. Playing Island first would give 5 mana total, leaving 2 mana open after Winternight Stories (3 mana) for Bounce Off or Burst Lightning as interaction. Additionally, with 8 instants/sorceries in graveyard, Eddymurk Crab costs just UU - playing land first and potentially casting Eddymurk Crab (a 5/5) could have been considered as an alternative line.

message: Discard a creature card instead of discarding two cards?
annotation_description: KimiK2 Valley discarded Eddymurk Crab as the second card for Winternight Stories. With 8 instants/sorceries already in the graveyard (Opt, Glacial Dragonhunt, Abandon Attachments, Winternight Stories x2, Spirebluff Canal - wait, let me recount: Opt, Glacial Dragonhunt, Abandon Attachments, Winternight Stories, Into the Flood Maw, Sleight of Hand = 6, plus the Winternight Stories resolving now adds more), the Eddymurk Crab's cost would be significantly reduced, making it a cheap 5/5 flash threat. Discarding it as a creature card would have satisfied the 'discard a creature card' clause, requiring only 1 discard instead of 2. The player chose to discard 2 non-creature cards (Riverpyre Verge and Eddymurk Crab) when they could have discarded just the Eddymurk Crab as a creature card to satisfy the alternative cost, saving a card.

Kimi25 Truth has Stormchaser's Talent at level 1 and exactly 4 mana available ({3}{U} cost to level up). Leveling up to level 2 would return an instant or sorcery from the graveyard to hand (though the graveyard only has Mountains and an Island, so actually there are no instant/sorcery targets in Kimi25's graveyard). However, the real consideration is sequencing: casting Winternight Stories before playing the Island from hand means spending 3 mana and only having 1 left, when playing Island first would give 5 mana available - enough to both cast Winternight Stories (3) and still have options. More importantly, with a Fish token and Frostcliff Siege (likely on Jeskai mode for card draw on combat damage), attacking first before casting sorceries would be better sequencing - cast spells post-combat to avoid telegraphing, and the Fish token dealing combat damage would draw a card via Frostcliff Siege Jeskai trigger. Casting the sorcery pre-combat before attacking is slightly suboptimal sequencing, though the prowess trigger on the Fish token from casting Winternight Stories before combat could help it survive blocks or deal more damage.

Cast Opt before playing the Island from hand. With the Island played first, KimiK2 Valley would have 5 mana available instead of 4, which opens up more options this turn (e.g., Winternight Stories at 3 mana + additional cantrips). There's no reason to hold the land drop.

Kimi25 Truth played Tiger-Seal in the postcombat main phase, meaning it will enter untapped but then tap at the beginning of their next upkeep anyway (Tiger-Seal's upkeep trigger). More importantly, they should have played Duelist of the Mind first. Duelist of the Mind has flying and vigilance with power equal to cards drawn this turn, and benefits from being on board to trigger its crime ability. Additionally, casting Tiger-Seal before playing a land drop is suboptimal sequencing - they have Island in hand and could play it first to have more mana available for responses. The bigger issue is that Stormchaser's Talent has an Otter token on the battlefield (from its ETB) that could have attacked during combat, but combat was skipped entirely. However, looking at the board state, no creatures are listed on Kimi25's battlefield, so the Otter token may have been removed earlier. Tiger-Seal itself is fine as a play, but Duelist of the Mind would likely have been the stronger creature to deploy given its evasion and synergy with the draw-heavy deck.

Playing a basic Island during postcombat main (when untapped mana doesn't matter) instead of Spirebluff Canal (which would enter tapped due to having 4+ other lands). By playing the Island now when untapped mana is irrelevant, they waste the 'enters untapped' advantage. Spirebluff Canal will always enter tapped from now on, so playing it during a phase where tapped vs untapped doesn't matter preserves a basic Island for a future turn where entering untapped could be relevant.

Cast Winternight Stories before cheaper cantrips (Opt/Sleight of Hand). Casting a 1-mana cantrip first would provide information to make better discard decisions for Winternight Stories. With 5 mana available, casting Sleight of Hand (1) then Winternight Stories (3) leaves 1 mana for Opt, giving maximum information for discard choices.

Cast Winternight Stories via Harmonize from graveyard for 5 mana (using all mana) instead of first playing Riverpyre Verge to have 6 mana total, or better yet casting it from hand for only 3 mana. Casting from hand for {2}{U} would leave 3 mana open (or 4 with the land drop) to hold up Spell Pierce and other interaction against an opponent with threatening board presence (Tiger-Seal, Duelist of the Mind, Frostcliff Siege). The Harmonize version also exiles the card, while the hand version keeps a copy in the graveyard for future Harmonize use.

message: Select card to discard (selected 0 of 3, min 3)
annotation_description: Discarded Steam Vents (which can enter untapped for 2 life) instead of Spirebluff Canal (which will always enter tapped with 5+ lands already on board). Steam Vents is strictly better than Spirebluff Canal at this stage of the game.

Casting Quantum Riddler (5 mana) during main phase when the opponent is tapped out is reasonable for the card advantage and body, but it leaves Kimi25 Truth with no mana open to protect their board or counter threats. With Spell Snare and Into the Flood Maw in hand, and a strong board already (Duelist of the Mind + Frostcliff Siege Jeskai for card draw on combat damage), there's an argument for playing a land, attacking with the current board to draw cards off Frostcliff Siege triggers, and holding up countermagic/interaction. However, the opponent is completely tapped out with 5 lands, so the window to safely deploy a 4/6 flyer is actually quite good. The main concern is that casting a creature before combat means Duelist of the Mind's power won't benefit from the Quantum Riddler draw trigger until after ETB resolves, and committing all mana main phase leaves no protection for the rest of the turn cycle.

message: Select card to discard (selected 0 of 2, min 2)
annotation_description: Discarded Multiversal Passage over Spirebluff Canal. With 5+ lands already on the battlefield, Spirebluff Canal will always enter tapped, while Multiversal Passage can enter untapped (for 2 life) and choose any basic land type. If a 6th land is ever needed, Multiversal Passage is strictly superior.

The player chose to play an Island (land drop) instead of casting Quantum Riddler, which is a powerful 4/6 flyer that draws a card on entry. With 4 lands untapped (Spirebluff Canal, Island, Riverpyre Verge, Island) plus the land drop, they have access to 5 mana - exactly enough for Quantum Riddler's cost of {3}{U}{U}. The opponent has only 2 untapped lands (Riverpyre Verge and Island), making it very unlikely they can counter the Riddler. Playing the land first is correct sequencing, but the reasoning text suggests they're ONLY playing the land and passing on casting Riddler. However, looking more carefully at the choices and the 'Chosen: ?' format - the player chose 'Island' (index 2) which is playing a land. This is actually fine sequencing IF they then cast Quantum Riddler afterward. But the confused reasoning about Quantum Riddler being a 'phantom' or 'glitch' suggests the player may not intend to cast it. More importantly, the player should play the land first (correct) and then cast Quantum Riddler with their 5 mana. Playing the land is the right first step, but if this is the only action taken this turn, it's a significant missed opportunity. Given the Warp cost of {1}{U} is also available, and the opponent is tapped out on 3 of 5 lands, this was the ideal time to deploy the threat. The reasoning clearly indicates confusion about Quantum Riddler and intent to just play a land.

Passed the postcombat main phase without playing a land. They have Island and Spirebluff Canal in hand with 6 lands on the battlefield. Playing a 7th land (Island entering untapped) would provide more mana next turn for Quantum Riddler or holding up more interaction, at zero cost.

KimiK2 Valley cast Eddymurk Crab before playing Spirebluff Canal from hand. They have 5 lands in play and Spirebluff Canal in hand - playing the land first would give 6 mana sources available. While Eddymurk Crab likely costs very little due to the 22 instants/sorceries in graveyard (costing only UU with that many), playing the land first is strictly better sequencing since it leaves more mana open after casting the Crab. With Spell Pierce in hand, having an extra mana available after deploying the Crab could matter for protecting it or interacting with the opponent's response.

Eddymurk Crab's ETB was used to tap KimiK2's own Eddymurk Crab and the opponent's Tiger-Seal, instead of tapping the opponent's two threatening creatures (Duelist of the Mind and Tiger-Seal). Tapping your own 5/5 flyer prevents attacking, and leaving Duelist of the Mind untapped means the opponent's flying vigilance threat remains available to both attack and block. Tiger-Seal already taps at upkeep so tapping it has limited value compared to Duelist of the Mind.

It's the beginning of KimiK2 Valley's own turn 13 (not the opponent's upkeep), and the opponent has Tiger-Seal which taps at the beginning of their upkeep. KimiK2 Valley could have cast Burst Lightning targeting the Duelist of the Mind (a */3 whose power equals cards drawn this turn - currently 0/3 at start of turn, so 2 damage wouldn't kill it) or Tiger-Seal (3/3, also wouldn't die to 2 damage). However, casting Opt here during their own beginning step before their main phase is a missed opportunity - Opt at instant speed during their own upkeep/beginning step would let them see an extra card before deciding their main phase plays, and there's no reason to hold it since they have mana available. The reasoning mentions 'opponent's upkeep' but it's actually KimiK2 Valley's own turn beginning phase. While passing is not terrible, casting Opt here to dig for answers at 11 life facing two creatures is slightly better than waiting.

Used Fear of Missing Out's Delirium untap trigger on the opponent's tapped Eddymurk Crab (5/5), giving the opponent a blocker they didn't have, instead of untapping one of their own tapped/attacking creatures to deal additional damage in the extra combat phase. While it triggers Duelist of the Mind's crime ability for a loot, that minor upside is vastly outweighed by giving the opponent a 5/5 blocker and losing extra combat damage.

Discarded Quantum Riddler, a powerful 4/6 flying finisher with card draw that wasn't yet on the battlefield, when they had redundant copies of enchantments already in play (second Stormchaser's Talent or second Frostcliff Siege) or a land (Spirebluff Canal) that could have been discarded instead.

Into the Flood Maw targeting Eddymurk Crab would commit a crime, triggering Duelist of the Mind's draw/discard ability. Drawing a card would set Duelist's power to 1, allowing it to deal combat damage, which would then trigger Frostcliff Siege (Jeskai) to draw another card. This chain generates meaningful card advantage and also removes the opponent's 5/5 creature temporarily.

KimiK2 Valley is facing lethal across two combats due to Fear of Missing Out's delirium granting an extra combat phase. Total damage across both combats would be ~17, far exceeding their 11 life. They had 3 untapped lands and 2 Burst Lightnings in hand, which together deal 4 damage - enough to kill Fear of Missing Out (2/3) before it attacks, preventing the extra combat phase. Without the extra combat, only Duelist (2) + Quantum Riddler (4) = 6 damage, leaving them at 5 life.

KimiK2 Valley is at 3 life facing lethal combat damage from Tiger-Seal (3/3) and Duelist of the Mind (3/3) attacking unblocked. They have Eddymurk Crab (5/5) on the battlefield which could block one attacker, plus Burst Lightning in hand which could kill the other 3-toughness creature. They also have an Opt they could cast before blocks. Instead of blocking or using removal, they passed on casting instants during combat and took 3 damage from Tiger-Seal alone, going to 0 life. They had Burst Lightning available to kill Tiger-Seal or Duelist of the Mind before damage, and Eddymurk Crab to block the other. This was a survivable combat that they chose not to interact with.
